pl-l4d14c4-d1e115.summary: States that penance is not done only once but repeated often, and pardon given again and again, as many saints prove.
claims: Penance is repeated and pardon repeatedly given.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine against heretics who said penance avails only once for those sinning after baptism, lest remission incite sin: they say the Lord would be an inciter of evil if he always helps penitents and that sins please him; they err, since sins greatly displease him who is always ready to destroy them; if he loved them, he would not always destroy them.
claims: Repeated forgiveness does not incite sin.
God's readiness to destroy sin shows his hatred of it.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e127.summary: Quotes Augustine to Macedonius: some sin again after penance and reconciliation at the altar, yet God makes his sun rise on them and gives them no less of life and salvation; though the place of penance in the church is not granted them, God does not forget his patience. Who would tell such a one, who weeps more and lives better, that it will profit him nothing hereafter? God forbid such madness.
claims: Those who relapse after solemn penance can still profit from penance.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e134.summary: Quotes Chrysostom: God's mercy never spurns penance offered sincerely; even one who has reached the height of evil and wishes to return is gladly received; even if he cannot complete the full order of satisfaction, God accepts however brief a penance and does not let even a small conversion lose its reward.
claims: God accepts even brief and incomplete penance.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e140.summary: Notes that the same can be shown by example.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e143.summary: Cites David: forgiven adultery and murder through penance, he later sinned gravely in numbering the people; yet offering himself to the angel striking the people, 'what have these sheep done? let your hand be on me', he was judged worthy of sacrifice who seemed unworthy of absolution; no wonder, since Moses too blotted out sins by offering himself for the people.
claims: David was forgiven twice through penance.

pl-l4d14c4-d1e149.summary: Concludes that we rise from sins through penance not once but often, and true penance is done repeatedly. When Paul says no sacrifice for sins remains for those who sin willfully, he means no second sacrifice, since Christ had to suffer once, and no second baptism, but a second, third, and further penance remains, as Chrysostom explains against those who use this text to deny penance.
claims: We rise from sin through penance repeatedly.
Hebrews excludes a second baptism and sacrifice, not repeated penance.

pl-l4d14c4.summary: Proves from the saints that penance is repeated and pardon given again and again. Augustine rebukes heretics who said penance avails only once after baptism, lest remission incite sin; God, ever ready to destroy sins, shows how much they displease him. Augustine to Macedonius: even those who sin again after penance and reconciliation are not abandoned by God, and their renewed penance profits them. Chrysostom: God never spurns sincere penance and accepts even brief penance. David, forgiven adultery and murder, sinned again by numbering the people and was again forgiven, offering himself for the people. So we rise from sins by penance not once but often; Hebrews' 'no sacrifice remains' excludes a second baptism and sacrifice, not repeated penance, as Chrysostom says.
claims: Penance can be repeated and pardon given repeatedly.
God's readiness to forgive shows sin displeases him, not that he incites it.
God accepts even brief and imperfect penance.
Hebrews 10 excludes a second baptism and sacrifice, not repeated penance.
